judgment.rationale: Both are Class-3 Content statements (rank 2) under CG-2. The second SFI, 'Addition and subtraction up to 999' (under C-2.3, 'applies the four basic operations on numbers to solve real-life problems'), with LCs 'Add whole numbers up to 999' and 'Subtract whole numbers up to 999', supplies the core computational skill. The first SFI, 'Addition and subtraction problems involving money' (under C-2.4, 'Handles simple transactions involving money'), with LCs 'Solve addition/subtraction problems involving money', applies that same operation range to a contextual money setting (notes up to Rs 500 in the same source row context). Within the same class rank this is a substantive move from decontextualised computation to real-life contextual application, so proficiency with three-digit addition/subtraction supports success on money word problems; the reverse dependency is not supported. Shared wording and page proximity alone were not treated as sufficient; the C-2.3/C-2.4 competency texts and LC skill texts carry the judgment. Note that both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted evidence items each) and the CG/Competency ancestors lack developmental coordinates, so the applied-versus-core reading rests on the bounded excerpts available.

judgment.rationale: Both are Class-5 Content bullets (rank 4, equal) under the same Competency C-2.5 ('Identifies, describes and extends simple number patterns') and Curricular Goal CG-2. 'Palindrome numbers' (LCs: identify/describe/extend palindrome numbers) and 'Multiples and common multiples' (LCs: identify and find multiples of a given number; identify common multiples of two numbers) are distinct but coherent instances of the same competency work: recognising, describing and extending structured classes of numbers. Neither provides the conceptual foundation for the other — palindromes rest on digit-reversal structure while multiples rest on multiplicative structure — so no developmental direction is supported at equal rank, and same-rank buildsTowards would need substantive evidence not present here. The coherence is genuine same-competency reinforcement of number-pattern reasoning rather than generic wording overlap (the nomination's lexical overlap is weak: shared tokens 'numbers', 'identify'), so relatesTo is the appropriate symmetric judgment. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and ancestors carry merge/audit context; this limits but does not contradict the reading above.

judgment.rationale: Both Content SFIs are Class-4 (rank 3, resolved) bullets under Competency C-2.3 (relationships among operations, applying the four operations) and CG-2 (fluency with whole numbers and the four operations). 'Understanding multiplication by 10' (LC: understand multiplication of numbers by 10; tags multiplication, place value, ten) and 'Construction of multiplication facts' (LC: construct multiplication facts) are substantively coherent, complementary aspects of developing multiplication within the same class: one focuses on the place-value pattern of multiplying by ten, the other on building the multiplication fact repertoire. They reinforce each other meaningfully, but the bounded evidence (single-bullet texts, same rank, same source row/page, no stated sequencing or increased complexity) does not substantively establish that proficiency in either supports success in the other, so a same-rank developmental direction is not warranted. judgment.rationale: Both are Class-3 Content bullets (rank 2, same resolved Class coordinate) under Competency C-2.3 (relationships among operations) and CG-2. The first covers skip counting and construction of multiplication tables of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10 'through equal groups' (LCs: skip count by 2,3,4,5,10; construct multiplication tables through equal groups); the second covers construction of division facts 'through equal sharing/grouping and repeated subtraction' (LCs: construct division facts through equal sharing and grouping; through repeated subtraction). The same-rank developmental direction is supported by pair-specific content, not just shared wording: the equal-groups multiplicative structure and skip-counting/multiplication-table facts established in the first are precisely the facts and counting structure a learner draws on to construct division facts by equal sharing/grouping and by repeated subtraction (the inverse of skip counting), consistent with the parent competency's focus on relationships among operations. Shared hierarchy, page proximity, and the single shared token 'equal' alone were not treated as sufficient. Source excerpts for both endpoints are truncated and both carry upstream audit/merge context, so confidence is moderate.

judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under the same Competency C-2.2 (representing and comparing commonly used fractions as parts of a whole) and Curricular Goal CG-2.
